trigger_evals.query: I want to create the PRD for the clinic's medical appointment scheduling system.
Help me plan the requirements for our app's recurring subscription feature.
Let's define the scope of the PIX payment feature before we start coding.
I need to document what we're going to build for the notifications module before the team starts implementation.
We still haven't gathered the business rules or permissions for the new admin panel. Can you help me map that out?
How do I fix this React syntax error: Unexpected token '<' on line 42 of the Header.tsx component?
Write a TypeScript function to validate an email using regex.
Why is the Next.js build failing with 'Module not found: Can't resolve @/lib/utils'?

evals.prompt: I want to create the PRD for the clinic's medical appointment scheduling system.
evals.expected_output: The skill starts in interview mode, asking 2-3 questions per round about problem/context, personas, scope, business rules, dependencies, or success criteria, instead of generating the document directly in the first response.

assertions.text: The initial response asks discovery questions (problem, personas, scope, business rules, dependencies, or success criteria) and does NOT generate docs/prd.md right away
The round of questions contains at most 2-3 questions, not a long list covering every area at once
The skill does not treat the user's vague answers as definitive; it signals it will refine the questions instead of proceeding with assumptions

evals.prompt: Help me plan the requirements for our app's recurring subscription feature.
evals.expected_output: The skill conducts multiple interview rounds progressively covering problem/context, personas/use cases, scope, business rules, dependencies/integrations, and success criteria, adapting the next questions to previous answers, before summarizing and asking for confirmation to generate the PRD.

assertions.text: Over the course of the interview (not necessarily in the first round), the skill covers the 6 areas: problem/context, personas/use cases, scope, business rules/constraints, dependencies/integrations, and success criteria
Before generating docs/prd.md, the skill presents a summary of what it understood and asks for the user's explicit confirmation

evals.prompt: Let's define the scope of the PIX payment feature before we start coding. Assume we already aligned on problem, personas, scope, business rules, dependencies, and success criteria in previous rounds; you can generate the PRD now.
evals.expected_output: After alignment is confirmed, the skill generates docs/prd.md with exactly the template's sections (Overview and Problem, Personas and Use Cases, User Stories, Consumes & Provides, Dependency Graph and Execution Waves, Acceptance Criteria), with Consumes & Provides mapping real dependencies and the graph organized into Waves by dependency (not by the order they were discussed).

assertions.text: docs/prd.md contains the sections in order: Overview and Problem, Personas and Use Cases, User Stories, Consumes & Provides, Dependency Graph and Execution Waves, Acceptance Criteria
User Stories are organized by epic and follow the format 'As a [persona], I want [action], so that [benefit]', with IDs (e.g., US-1, US-2)
The Consumes & Provides section exists and maps, per feature/epic, at least one dependency (Consumes) and one exposure (Provides), even when the dependency seems obvious

The Waves in Dependency Graph and Execution Waves reflect real dependencies between features (a feature only enters Wave N if all its dependencies are in previous Waves), not the order they were discussed
Acceptance Criteria are objectively verifiable (Given/When/Then format or an objective checklist) and do not use vague terms like 'works well' or 'is fast'
After writing docs/prd.md, the skill shows a brief summary of the generated content and asks whether anything needs adjusting before moving on to tracking

evals.prompt: The PIX payment PRD (in docs/prd.md) has already been approved by the team. Can you generate the tracking file now?
evals.expected_output: The skill generates docs/progress.json listing one entry per feature/user story from the PRD, grouped by wave, each with an id matching the PRD, initial status 'pending', and dependsOn reflecting the document's dependency graph.

assertions.text: docs/progress.json is created referencing the same user story ids used in docs/prd.md (e.g., US-1)
All features listed in docs/progress.json have status 'pending', with none marked as 'in_progress' or 'done'
The dependsOn field of each feature in docs/progress.json matches the dependency graph described in docs/prd.md
Features in docs/progress.json are grouped by wave (the 'wave' field), consistent with the Waves defined in the PRD

evals.prompt: How do I fix this React syntax error: Unexpected token '<' on line 42 of the Header.tsx component?
evals.expected_output: The amdev:prd-writer skill is NOT triggered; the task is handled as code debugging, not product planning.

assertions.text: The amdev:prd-writer skill is not invoked; no product discovery question (problem/personas/scope) is asked

evals.prompt: Write a TypeScript function to validate an email using regex.
evals.expected_output: The amdev:prd-writer skill is NOT triggered; the task is direct code implementation.

assertions.text: The amdev:prd-writer skill is not invoked; the response delivers the requested function without a discovery interview

evals.prompt: Why is the Next.js build failing with 'Module not found: Can't resolve @/lib/utils'?
evals.expected_output: The amdev:prd-writer skill is NOT triggered; the task is configuration/build debugging, not product planning.

assertions.text: The amdev:prd-writer skill is not invoked; the response focuses on diagnosing the module resolution error, without starting a discovery interview
